text: This capstone used every chapter that came before it. Chapter 1's platform-as-a-product framing and Chapter 2's catalog and scaffolder concepts are the entire foundation of Lesson 29's golden-path template. Chapter 3's GitOps principles and Chapter 4's practice -- the Application reconciliation model especially -- carried both labs. Chapter 5's canary mechanics, Chapter 6's reusable pipelines, and Chapter 7's instrumentation each did real, specific work, not just background reading.

Lesson 29 didn't invent a catalog or a scaffolder -- it extended Chapter 2's catalog-info.yaml and template.yaml concepts into a real, runnable golden path with CI/CD and monitoring already wired in, and a pipeline that extends Chapter 6's shared template instead of defining its own. Lesson 30's canary rollout stayed GitOps start to finish because the Rollout and its AnalysisTemplate were just more YAML in the same overlay Chapter 4's Application model already reconciled.

Lesson 31's case study runs directly on Chapter 7 and Chapter 1. Northfield Retail's first failure was never instrumenting the platform or its users' experience, exactly what Chapter 7 teaches a platform team to do from day one. And its three failures -- no feedback loop, adoption by mandate, a golden path that didn't fit real teams -- are Chapter 1's warnings about platform as a product, played out concretely instead of left abstract.

Across four lessons, this capstone built one real golden-path template that scaffolds a new service correctly from the first commit, wired a GitOps-driven canary with automated rollback on a real metric, and examined what happens when all of that technical work is done right and adoption still doesn't follow. That's the real job of platform engineering -- not just building a correct platform, but building one that earns the adoption it needs to matter.

This course -- Advanced Platform Engineering, GitOps and CI/CD -- is complete, and it closes differently than most courses in this path. It's the first of four Expert Specialization courses that build on the earlier Advanced Specialization stage but not on each other, so there's no single next course. A student can take Hybrid and Multi-Cloud Enterprise Architecture, AI Cloud Infrastructure and MLOps, or Advanced SRE and Disaster Recovery next, in whatever order fits their goals.

Eight chapters of platform fundamentals, developer self-service, GitOps principles and practice, advanced CI/CD, pipeline-as-code at scale, and observability, proven on one real golden path and one real progressive-delivery rollout, and tested against a scenario where the technical work alone wasn't enough. Pick any of the other three Expert Specialization courses next.
